title: David's Secret Demons: Messiah, Murderer, Traitor, King
author: Baruch Halpern
allowedUseNotes: Modern copyrighted scholarly monograph. Project stores only its own summary/paraphrase of the book's argument, drawn from secondary description; no reproduction of its text.
summary: A critical scholarly reconstruction of David's rise that reads the History of David's Rise as apologetic literature answering specific, real accusations against David, reconstructed by Halpern from the shape of the text's own defensive insistences. As consistently described across independent secondary sources discussing the book, Halpern argues David himself bears responsibility for the deaths of a series of rivals and Saulide claimants — Abner, Ish-bosheth, and later Amasa among them — cleared from his path to the throne, with the narrative's repeated protestations of David's innocence read as evidence of exactly what they deny. This project cites Halpern, alongside McKenzie (mckenzie-2000-king-david), as a named, checkable proponent of the political rival-elimination reading of Abner's death (claim-abner-killing's view-abner-killing-rival-elimination).
confidenceNotes: Verified via secondary/web-search cross-corroboration only (not primary-copy inspection): the book's existence, author, publisher, and 2001 publication date are independently corroborated across Eerdmans' own listing, Amazon, Barnes & Noble, Goodreads, and multiple reviews (including The Gospel Coalition's Themelios review and a DTS Voice review) describing its argument that David was 'the guilty party in the assassinations of Abner, Amasa, and Ishbosheth.'
